Let $i\in I$ and let $T_{i,c,t}$ be the toral quantum binomials of
[[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]]
($i\in I$, $c\in\mathbb Z$, $t\ge0$, $T_{i,c,0}=1$), inside the Drinfeld–Jimbo
algebra $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ of [[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]
with $U_A$ and its parts $U_A^-,U_A^0,U_A^+$ as in that definition. Write
$E=E_i$, $F=F_i$, $E^{(a)}=E_i^{(a)}$, $F^{(b)}=F_i^{(b)}$ for the divided
powers of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]] and put
$q=q_i$ inside the displayed formulas.

(i) **Divided-power multiplication.** For all $a,b\ge0$,
$$E^{(a)}E^{(b)}=\binom{a+b}{a}_iE^{(a+b)},\qquad F^{(a)}F^{(b)}=\binom{a+b}{a}_iF^{(a+b)}.$$

(ii) **Toral recursion and commutation.** For $t\ge1$,
$$T_{i,c,t}=\frac{K_iq_i^{\,c-t+1}-K_i^{-1}q_i^{\,-c+t-1}}{q_i^{\,t}-q_i^{\,-t}}\,T_{i,c,t-1}.$$
Each $T_{i,c,t}$ is a Laurent polynomial in $K_i^{\pm1}$ with coefficients in
$\mathbb Q(q)$; the toral elements commute with one another and with all $K_h$.
For all $i,j$ and all $m\in\mathbb Z$ one has
$K_i^{\,m}T_{j,c,t}=T_{j,c,t}K_i^{\,m}$ if $i\ne j$, while
$E_iT_{i,c,t}=T_{i,c-2,t}E_i$, $E_jT_{i,c,t}=T_{i,c-a_{ij},t}E_j$,
$F_iT_{i,c,t}=T_{i,c+2,t}F_i$, $F_jT_{i,c,t}=T_{i,c+a_{ij},t}F_j$ for all $j$.
In particular $E_iT_{i,c,t}\in U_A^0E_i$, $F_iT_{i,c,t}\in U_A^0F_i$,
$T_{i,c,t}E_i=E_iT_{i,c+2,t}\in E_iU_A^0$ and
$T_{i,c,t}F_i=F_iT_{i,c-2,t}\in F_iU_A^0$: the toral factor can be moved to the
middle at the cost of a shift of the binomial index.

(iii) **Reordering identity.** For all $a,b\ge0$,
$$E_i^{(a)}F_i^{(b)}=\sum_{t=0}^{\min(a,b)}F_i^{(b-t)}\,T_{i,\,2t-a-b,\,t}\,E_i^{(a-t)},$$
with every coefficient a toral quantum binomial in $U_A^0$. In particular
$E_iF_i-F_iE_i=T_{i,0,1}$ and
$E_i^{(a)}F_i^{(a)}=\sum_{t=0}^{a}F_i^{(a-t)}T_{i,2t-2a,t}E_i^{(a-t)}$.
For $i\ne j$, $E_i^{(a)}$ and $F_j^{(b)}$ commute; the same-half divided powers
$E_i^{(a)},E_j^{(b)}$ (and likewise $F_i^{(a)},F_j^{(b)}$) commute whenever
$a_{ij}=0$, and for $a_{ij}\ne0$ no commutation is asserted.

(iv) **Triangular spanning.** Every element of $U_A$ is an $A$-linear
combination of products $b_-u\,b_+$ with $b_-\in U_A^-$, $u\in U_A^0$ and
$b_+\in U_A^+$; equivalently $U_A=U_A^-U_A^0U_A^+$ as an $A$-module. No
independence of the spanning family is asserted.

Let $B_K$ be the normalized Kashiwara half form on $U_q^-$ of [[thm-the-negative-half-bilinear-form-is-symmetric-nondegenerate-and-integral]], with skew derivations $e_i',e_i''$ of [[def-kashiwara-skew-derivations-on-the-negative-quantum-half]], and let $\psi$ be the bar involution of [[lem-the-lusztig-integral-form-is-stable-under-bar-and-contravariant-duality]]. Then:

(i) **Parameter transport.** The assignment $\varphi(v)=q^{-1}$, $\varphi(E_i^L)=E_i$, $\varphi(F_i^L)=F_i$, $\varphi(K_h^L)=K_{-h}$ defines an algebra isomorphism semilinear for the field isomorphism $\mathbb Q(v)\to\mathbb Q(q)$, $v\mapsto q^{-1}$. Its inverse sends $q\mapsto v^{-1}$ and $K_h\mapsto K_{-h}^L$, fixing the root generators. After the separate coefficient-renaming isomorphism $\rho:v\mapsto q$, $K_h^L\mapsto K_h$, this transport is $\varphi=\psi\rho$, with $\psi$ the library bar involution. It carries the source integral form onto $U_A$, fixes divided powers, inverts toral generators and fixes $T_{i,c,t}$. One must not apply the library bar a second time to the already transported parameter $v=q^{-1}$.

(ii) **Coproduct transport.** On all of the source algebra, $(\varphi\otimes\varphi)\circ\Delta_L=\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\circ\varphi$, where $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}=\mathrm{flip}\circ\Delta$. Equivalently the source coproduct is the opposite of the fixed library coproduct after parameter transport: the flip of the transported source coproduct is $\Delta$. In particular, with the barred coproduct $\bar\Delta(u):=(\psi\otimes\psi)\Delta(\psi(u))$, an element of the completed tensor square satisfying the source intertwining convention for $\Delta_L$ has a transport-flip that satisfies the library convention $\Delta(u)\Theta=\Theta\bar\Delta(u)$; this is the convention under which the normalized family of (vi) is read.

(iii) **The abstract half and its twisted product.** Transporting $\theta_i\mapsto F_i$ sends the source half $\mathbf f$ to $U_q^-$, the divided powers $\theta_i^{(n)}$ to $F_i^{(n)}$, and the source twisted coproduct multiplication $(x_1\otimes x_2)(y_1\otimes y_2)=v^{\langle\deg x_2,\deg y_1\rangle}x_1y_1\otimes x_2y_2$ to
$$(x_1\otimes x_2)(y_1\otimes y_2)=q^{-\langle\deg x_2,\deg y_1\rangle}x_1y_1\otimes x_2y_2$$
on $U_q^-\otimes U_q^-$; the coefficient extraction $e_i'(F_jQ)=\delta_{ij}Q+q_i^{-a_{ij}}F_je_i'(Q)$ of the transported twisted coproduct agrees with the library skew derivation $e_i'$.

(iv) **The half form up to the root-color factor.** On the homogeneous degree $\nu=\sum_i\nu_i\alpha_i$ the source form and the normalized Kashiwara form are related by
$$B_L=C_\nu\,B_K,\qquad C_\nu=\prod_i(1-q_i^2)^{-\nu_i},$$
a color-degree scaling which is a unit congruent to $1$ modulo $q$ and is not a single scalar on the whole half; for $P,Q$ of different degrees both sides vanish. In the rank-one subalgebra $B_L(F_i^{(n)},F_i^{(n)})=\prod_{r=1}^n(1-q_i^{2r})^{-1}$.

(v) **The normalized Drinfeld pairing.** Let $\iota:U_q^+\to U_q^-$ be the algebra isomorphism $E_i\mapsto F_i$. On homogeneous elements of opposite degrees set
$$D(x,y)=d_\nu^{-1}B_K(\iota x,y),\qquad d_\nu=\prod_i(q_i-q_i^{-1})^{\nu_i}\ \ (\deg x=\nu,\ \deg y=-\nu),$$
and set $D(x,y)=0$ for degrees not opposite. Then $D$ is a well-defined homogeneous pairing, perfect on every finite graded piece, and $D(E_i,F_j)=\delta_{ij}/(q_i-q_i^{-1})$; the pairing with generator value $1$ is the $B_K$-transport $B_K(\iota x,y)$. Its divided-power values are
$$D(E_i^{(n)},F_i^{(n)})=\frac{q_i^{-n(n-1)/2}}{[n]_i!\,(q_i-q_i^{-1})^n}.$$

(vi) **Quasi-R normalization.** In each degree $\nu$ let $(x_a),(y_b)$ be bases of $U_q^+[\nu]$ and $U_q^-[-\nu]$ and let $\Theta_\nu=\sum_a x_a\otimes y^a$ be the $D$-coevaluation, $y^a$ the $D$-dual basis. Then $\Theta_\nu$ is the transported, tensor-flipped source quasi-R component: the source coefficient of Lusztig's printed $\Theta$ is $(-1)^{\mathrm{ht}\,\nu}\prod_iv_i^{\nu_i}$ times the $B_L$-coevaluation, and after parameter transport and flip this scalar equals $d_\nu$, the scalar by which the $D$-coevaluation differs from the $B_K$-coevaluation. In particular, writing $[n]_{q_i^2}!=\prod_{r=1}^n(1+q_i^2+\cdots+q_i^{2(r-1)})$ (the geometric-sum factorial of the receiving page),
$$\Theta_{n\alpha_i}=(q_i-q_i^{-1})^n[n]_{q_i^2}!\,E_i^{(n)}\otimes F_i^{(n)},\qquad\text{so}\qquad \Theta_{\alpha_i}=(q_i-q_i^{-1})\,E_i\otimes F_i.$$

Let $\lambda\in P$ be a dominant integral label weight, put
$m_i:=\langle\lambda,h_i\rangle\ge0$, and let $M(\lambda)$ be the quantum Verma
module with highest vector $v_\lambda$
([[def-quantum-verma-module-and-simple-highest-weight-quotient]],

$\lambda-Q_+$, is integrable, and equals the canonical simple highest weight
module $L(\lambda)$, which is simple also as an ordinary (not assumed graded)
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module.

(ii) **Universality.** Every integrable cyclic highest weight module $V$ of
highest weight $\lambda$ with highest vector $v\ne0$ receives a
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module map $\tilde L(\lambda)\to V$ with
$\bar v_\lambda\mapsto v$, and this map is unique; every nonzero such $V$ is
isomorphic to $L(\lambda)$.

(iii) Its character equals the classical integrable highest weight character of
the explicitly regularized realization of the datum. No global
$\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-freeness and no crystal or global basis is used.

No commutation between divided powers $F_i^{(a)},F_j^{(b)}$ of distinct indices

Let $T$ and $I_{\mathrm{DJ}}$ be the free algebra and defining ideal of
[[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]], and put
$m_{ij}=1-a_{ij}$ and $\mathrm{Serre}^{\pm}_{ij}$ for its displayed Serre
sums. Define $\omega,\psi,\tau:T\to T$ on generators by

$$\omega(E_i)=-F_i,\quad\omega(F_i)=-E_i,\quad\omega(K_h)=K_{-h},$$

$$\psi(E_i)=E_i,\quad\psi(F_i)=F_i,\quad\psi(K_h)=K_{-h},$$

$$\tau(E_i)=F_i,\quad\tau(F_i)=E_i,\quad\tau(K_h)=K_{-h}.$$

Here $\omega$ fixes $\mathbb Q(q)$, while $\psi$ and $\tau$ apply the field
involution $q\mapsto q^{-1}$ to coefficients; $\omega$ and $\psi$ extend as
algebra maps, and $\tau$ extends as an anti-algebra map. Each map preserves
$I_{\mathrm{DJ}}$ and descends to $U_q(\mathfrak g)$. All three are
involutions; $\omega$ is a $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra automorphism, $\psi$ a
semilinear algebra automorphism, and $\tau$ a semilinear algebra
anti-involution. On the Serre sums,

$$\omega(\mathrm{Serre}^{\pm}_{ij})=(-1)^{a_{ij}}\mathrm{Serre}^{\mp}_{ij},\qquad\psi(\mathrm{Serre}^{\pm}_{ij})=\mathrm{Serre}^{\pm}_{ij},\qquad\tau(\mathrm{Serre}^{\pm}_{ij})=(-1)^{1-a_{ij}}\mathrm{Serre}^{\mp}_{ij}.$$

Let $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra of a finite symmetrizable Cartan datum, over $k=\mathbb Q(q)$, and let $U_q^-,U_q^0,U_q^+$ be its generated subalgebras of [[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]].

(i) Multiplication is a vector-space isomorphism
$$m:U_q^-\otimes_k U_q^0\otimes_k U_q^+\longrightarrow U_q(\mathfrak g),\qquad x_-\otimes x_0\otimes x_+\longmapsto x_-x_0x_+.$$
Products $b_-K_h b_+$, with $b_\pm$ ranging over supplied bases of the two halves and $h\in P^\vee$, form a basis of $U_q(\mathfrak g)$. Arbitrary simple-generator words span the halves; their Serre relations preclude claiming their independence.

(ii) The halves are exactly the algebras presented by their separate Serre relations, and $U_q^0\cong k[P^\vee]$. Thus all three abstract factor maps are injective and the $K_h$ are linearly independent.

(iii) For every $\beta\in Q$, the total root grading satisfies
$$U_q(\mathfrak g)[\beta]\cong\bigoplus_{\alpha,\gamma\in Q_+,\,\alpha-\gamma=\beta} U_q^-[-\gamma]\otimes_k U_q^0\otimes_k U_q^+[\alpha].$$
In particular degree zero contains all equal-positive/negative-degree summands, including $F_iE_i$; it is not just the toral subalgebra. As a left $U_q^0$-module this component is free, with rank equal to the possibly infinite sum of the products of the two half-component dimensions. Under AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the half-component dimensions are their classical PBW ranks, and products of the generic PBW bases of [[thm-generic-quantum-serre-halves-have-classical-pbw-ranks-and-a-nondegenerate-hopf-pairing]] with the toral basis give a PBW basis of the whole algebra. **Finite-type universal coefficients (c).** In finite Cartan type choose a longest Weyl element $w_0$ and sufficiently large regular dominant weights as in [F4]. The unsigned Chevalley map $\omega$ commutes with the normalized bar, so the normalized field isomorphism from the corresponding lowest module to the highest module is a form isometry and bar compatible, and its source integral lattice maps into the target because the extremal vector is integral and $U_A$-stable. **The constructed highest and lowest classes (d).** Form right-associated products of highest modules. Highest-first action proves integrality of the normalized bar at every binary step, while the field cocycle of [F2] gives all parenthesizations the same bar without assuming integral action for intermediate arbitrary pairs. In the transfer order in which each positive-root component raises the first weight and lowers the second, only the degree-$0$ component fixes a label pair, so the bar is triangular with diagonal $1$. Every upward interval is finite by the upper-cone or finite-total-weight hypothesis, and for the lowest classes the lower-cone bound replaces finiteness of the whole mixed weight space. In a finite interval solve for a bar-fixed lift $g_t=e_t+\sum_{s>t}a_{ts}e_s$ with $a_{ts}\in q\mathbb Z[q]$, starting from the top: after subtracting the already constructed larger lifts, involutivity makes the remainder satisfy $f+\bar f=0$, whose unique positive $q$-part supplies the next correction. Finite induction gives existence, uniqueness and a unitriangular $A$-matrix with finite-interval inverse; the corrected family is an $A$-basis and an $A_0$-basis with the raw tensor crystal residues, is bar fixed, and has $A_\infty$-span the actual tensor bar chart.

**Closure under tensor constructions and based subquotients.** For a highest tensor object $P=V(\lambda_1)\otimes\cdots\otimes V(\lambda_m)$ and any based $N$, right-associate $P\otimes N$. Repeated highest-first action from step 1.1 makes every binary bar integral. The cocycle identifies this bar with the grouped one using the constructed bar of $P$, so $\Theta$ acts integrally on $P\otimes N$. The mirror argument uses step 1.2 for arbitrary first factor and a lowest tensor object. This includes pairs of constructed objects and proves the arbitrary-other-factor cases before inheritance. Based subobjects are spanned by subsets of the actual constructed bases and are therefore saturated, $(P_A\otimes Q_A)\cap(P'\otimes Q')=P'_A\otimes Q'_A$; $\Theta$ preserves their field submodules by its $U$-monomial terms, so integral action follows from the equality. Based quotient maps are $U$-linear, send basis to basis or $0$, have basis-subset kernel and commute with bars because both bars fix those bases; their integral tensor maps are surjective onto free complementary quotient lattices, so integral action descends. Direct sums are handled componentwise with the stated weight bounds. This proves closure of $C_{\mathrm{high}}$ and, dually, of $C_{\mathrm{low}}$, hence (d) for the pure classes, and for an ordered highest-prefix, based-middle, lowest-suffix product each binary split has either a pure highest-class left block or a pure lowest-class right block, so one of the two action cases applies; every prefix transfer is bounded by a prefix upper cone or a complementary lowest suffix lower cone, so all correction intervals are finite.

**The affine boundaries.** For $A_1^{(1)}$, with $a_{01}=a_{10}=-2$, the degree-$\delta$ Kashiwara Gram matrix in the basis $F_0F_1,F_1F_0$ is $\begin{pmatrix}1&q^2\\q^2&1\end{pmatrix}$, so the correct $D$-coevaluation carries the factor $(q-q^{-1})^2/(1-q^4)=q^{-2}(1-q^2)/(1+q^2)\notin A$: the universal algebra-coefficient claim fails in affine type. For the stronger arbitrary-pair failure take $\lambda=\Lambda_0$, $\mu=\lambda-\delta$, $p=[2]$, and the global element $g=F_1F_0v_\lambda$; then $E_0g=0$, $E_1g=pF_0v$, $F_0^{(r)}g=0$ for $r\ge2$ by the length-three divided Serre relation, and $F_1g=pF_1^{(2)}F_0v$, $F_1^{(r)}g=0$ for $r\ge2$ by its rank-one length-two string. The integral based-quotient presentation therefore gives a $U_A$-map $V_A(\mu)/p\to V_A(\lambda)/p$ sending the highest vector to $g\bmod p$. For each global $h_b$ its image has bar-fixed coefficients in $A/(p)=\mathbb Z[i]$, whose bar-fixed subring is $\mathbb Z$; let $T_b$ be its unique integer-coordinate lift in the $\lambda$-global basis and set $c_b=h_b+T_b/p$. The free module $M_A$ with basis $\mathcal B_\lambda\cup\{c_b\}$ inside $V_\lambda\oplus V_\mu$ is $U_A$-stable because $UT_b-T(Uh_b)$ is divisible by $p$, all basis vectors are homogeneous and bar fixed, and because $1/p=q/(1+q^2)\in qA_0$ its exact chart and residue data equal the standard direct-sum based module, so all four based axioms hold. On the tensor $c_{\mathrm{top}}\otimes h_\mu$ the $\Theta$-action has the term $c_{\mathrm{top}}\otimes h_\mu-\frac{1-q^2}{1+q^2}v_\lambda\otimes g_\mu$, whose coefficient is not in $A$ and lies on a distinct tensor basis vector (the simple-root terms vanish by the displayed relations and every higher first raising degree vanishes). Hence unrestricted arbitrary-based $O_{\mathrm{int}}$ action is false, and the ordered or constructed hypotheses of (a)–(d) are necessary.

**Finite-type action does not imply supported globalization.** In [F6] every algebraic normalized lift of the specified seed would have finite raw support and coefficients in $q\mathbb Z[q]$ away from its seed. Project such a bar-fixed lift to a cut $J$ greater than its maximal constituent index by two. The projection has the same normalization, and finite-cut uniqueness in [F6] identifies it with the cut lift. That lift has a nonzero coordinate at constituent index at least $J-1$, outside the putative finite support, a contradiction. Thus the unrestricted construction assertion fails even in rank one, although the evaluated quasi-$R$ action is finite and integral. For balancedness, any element $g$ of the natural integral zero/bar intersection has both $g$ and $\Psi g$ with polynomial raw coefficients. The finite difference $w=\Psi g-g$ is anti-invariant; at its least first weight strict triangularity gives $\bar s=-s$ for a polynomial coefficient $s$, forcing $s=0$ and therefore $w=0$. Consequently a balanced seed lift would be such a finite fixed lift and is impossible. The residue condition and the least-first-weight argument eliminate all polynomial corrections at or below the seed weight, so such a balanced lift has the triangular normalization just contradicted. Finite-dimensional based pairs remain fully covered: their entire raw tensor basis is a finite correction closure. More generally integral finite-column triangularity with finite raw-basis correction closure gives the same finite correction and inverse used in step 2.2. This leaves all supported constructions of step 3.1 intact.

**Conclusion.** Steps 1.1–1.2 prove the highest-first and lowest-second action with integral lattice preservation; step 1.3 proves arbitrary-multiplicity finite-type action finiteness; step 2.1 proves the finite-type algebra coefficients $\Theta_
u\in U_A^+[
u]\otimes U_A^-[-
u]$; steps 2.2–3.1 construct the corrected tensor global basis, prove its triangularity with diagonal $1$ and establish the bounded highest/lowest construction and closure classes in (d); step 4.1 records the exact affine failure of the unrestricted statements. Step 4.2 refutes only the unrestricted supported-globalization inference from case (c). The only Choice use is [C1].

powers of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]] and put
$q=q_i$ inside the displayed formulas.

(i) **Divided-power multiplication.** For all $a,b\ge0$,
$$E^{(a)}E^{(b)}=\binom{a+b}{a}_iE^{(a+b)},\qquad F^{(a)}F^{(b)}=\binom{a+b}{a}_iF^{(a+b)}.$$

(ii) **Toral recursion and commutation.** For $t\ge1$,
$$T_{i,c,t}=\frac{K_iq_i^{\,c-t+1}-K_i^{-1}q_i^{\,-c+t-1}}{q_i^{\,t}-q_i^{\,-t}}\,T_{i,c,t-1}.$$
Each $T_{i,c,t}$ is a Laurent polynomial in $K_i^{\pm1}$ with coefficients in
$\mathbb Q(q)$; the toral elements commute with one another and with all $K_h$.
For all $i,j$ and all $m\in\mathbb Z$ one has
$K_i^{\,m}T_{j,c,t}=T_{j,c,t}K_i^{\,m}$ if $i\ne j$, while
$E_iT_{i,c,t}=T_{i,c-2,t}E_i$, $E_jT_{i,c,t}=T_{i,c-a_{ij},t}E_j$,
$F_iT_{i,c,t}=T_{i,c+2,t}F_i$, $F_jT_{i,c,t}=T_{i,c+a_{ij},t}F_j$ for all $j$.
In particular $E_iT_{i,c,t}\in U_A^0E_i$, $F_iT_{i,c,t}\in U_A^0F_i$,
$T_{i,c,t}E_i=E_iT_{i,c+2,t}\in E_iU_A^0$ and
$T_{i,c,t}F_i=F_iT_{i,c-2,t}\in F_iU_A^0$: the toral factor can be moved to the
middle at the cost of a shift of the binomial index.

(iii) **Reordering identity.** For all $a,b\ge0$,
$$E_i^{(a)}F_i^{(b)}=\sum_{t=0}^{\min(a,b)}F_i^{(b-t)}\,T_{i,\,2t-a-b,\,t}\,E_i^{(a-t)},$$
with every coefficient a toral quantum binomial in $U_A^0$. In particular
$E_iF_i-F_iE_i=T_{i,0,1}$ and
$E_i^{(a)}F_i^{(a)}=\sum_{t=0}^{a}F_i^{(a-t)}T_{i,2t-2a,t}E_i^{(a-t)}$.
For $i\ne j$, $E_i^{(a)}$ and $F_j^{(b)}$ commute; the same-half divided powers
$E_i^{(a)},E_j^{(b)}$ (and likewise $F_i^{(a)},F_j^{(b)}$) commute whenever
$a_{ij}=0$, and for $a_{ij}\ne0$ no commutation is asserted.

(iv) **Triangular spanning.** Every element of $U_A$ is an $A$-linear
combination of products $b_-u\,b_+$ with $b_-\in U_A^-$, $u\in U_A^0$ and
$b_+\in U_A^+$; equivalently $U_A=U_A^-U_A^0U_A^+$ as an $A$-module. No
independence of the spanning family is asserted.

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum for a quantum
group with $a_{ii}=2$ for all $i$
([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]), let
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be its Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra
([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]) with $q_i=q^{d_i}$ and
$K_i=K_{d_ih_i}$, and set

$$A:=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]\ \subseteq\ \mathbb Q(q),$$

the image of the Laurent polynomial ring $\Lambda_1=\mathbb Z[t]_{S}$ of
[[def-the-laurent-polynomial-ring]] under the unital ring homomorphism sending
$t$ to the indeterminate $q$; this homomorphism is injective and $A$ is a
subring of $\mathbb Q(q)$ (Verification, step 1.1). We work over this
commutative domain $A$ inside the field $\mathbb Q(q)$.

For $i\in I$, $c\in\mathbb Z$ and $t\ge0$ define the **toral quantum binomial**

$$T_{i,c,t}:=\begin{bmatrix}K_i;c\\ t\end{bmatrix}:=\prod_{s=1}^{t}\frac{K_iq_i^{\,c-s+1}-K_i^{-1}q_i^{\,-c+s-1}}{q_i^{\,s}-q_i^{\,-s}}\in U_q(\mathfrak g),$$

the empty product being $T_{i,c,0}:=1$. Each factor is defined in
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$ because $q_i^{\,s}-q_i^{\,-s}\ne0$ for $s\ge1$
([[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]), so
$T_{i,c,t}$ is a polynomial in $K_i^{\pm1}$ with coefficients in $\mathbb Q(q)$;
in particular all $T_{i,c,t}$ commute with the $K_h$ and with one another
(Verification, step 2.1).

The **Lusztig divided-power integral form** is the $A$-subalgebra

$$U_A:=\bigl\langle E_i^{(r)},\ F_i^{(r)},\ K_h^{\pm1},\ T_{i,c,t}\ \colon\ i\in I,\ r,t\ge0,\ c\in\mathbb Z,\ h\in P^{\vee}\bigr\rangle\ \subseteq\ U_q(\mathfrak g),$$

where $x^{(r)}=x^r/[r]_i!$ are the divided powers of
[[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]. Write $U_A^\pm$
for the $A$-subalgebras generated by the $E_i^{(r)}$ and by the $F_i^{(r)}$,
and $U_A^0$ for the one generated by the $K_h^{\pm1}$ and the $T_{i,c,t}$.

Then:

(i) $U_A$ contains $E_i=E_i^{(1)}$, $F_i=F_i^{(1)}$ and all $K_h$;

(ii) $U_A$ is a root-graded $A$-subalgebra of the root-graded
$\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ ([[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]):
with $U_A[\beta]:=U_A\cap U_q(\mathfrak g)[\beta]$ one has
$U_A=\bigoplus_{\beta\in Q}U_A[\beta]$, each $U_A[\beta]$ is an $A$-submodule,
and $U_A^\pm,U_A^0$ are graded in the same way;

(iii) $U_A\otimes_A\mathbb Q(q)\cong U_q(\mathfrak g)$ canonically, i.e. the
$\mathbb Q(q)$-span of $U_A$ is all of $U_q(\mathfrak g)$.

The shifted binomials $T_{i,c,t}$ with $c\ne0$ are included because the
divided-power reordering identity of
[[lem-divided-power-and-toral-quantum-binomial-reordering-identities]] has
coefficients $T_{i,2t-a-b,t}$ with a nonconstant index; the specializations at
$q=1$ of these elements are computed in
[[lem-q-one-toral-specialization-identifies-the-classical-cartan-generators]],
and the integral triangular decomposition and the specialization are treated
only after this definition.

No freeness of $U_A$ or of its parts over $A$, no independence of the listed
generators, and no triangularity of the products of the three parts is asserted
here. In particular $A$ is not a principal ideal domain (Verification, step
7.1), so no torsion-free-to-free inference over $A$ is permitted anywhere on
this page.

In the same positive-first/negative-second completion $\widehat C$ of [[def-root-height-completion-for-weightwise-quasi-r-intertwiners]], let $\Theta=\sum_\nu\Theta_\nu$ be the unique normalized bar-coproduct intertwiner of [[thm-the-weightwise-quasi-r-intertwiner-exists-and-is-unique]]. Then:

(i) $\Theta^{-1}=\overline\Theta=(\psi\otimes\psi)(\Theta)$, the inverse being taken in the root-height convolution algebra of $\widehat C$ and not switching the positive and negative tensor order;

(ii) for every $\nu$ the exact threefold identities hold:
$$(\Delta\otimes\mathrm{id})\Theta_\nu=\sum_{\gamma+\eta=\nu}(\Theta_\gamma)_{23}(1\otimes K_{-\eta}\otimes1)(\Theta_\eta)_{13},$$
$$(\mathrm{id}\otimes\Delta)\Theta_\nu=\sum_{\gamma+\eta=\nu}(\Theta_\gamma)_{12}(1\otimes K_\eta\otimes1)(\Theta_\eta)_{13},$$
with subscripts denoting tensor positions and $\Theta_{\nu'}=0$ when $\nu'\notin Q_+$;

(iii) the two normalized tensor-bar compositions satisfy the field cocycle identity
$$((\Delta\otimes\mathrm{id})\Theta)\Theta_{12}=((\mathrm{id}\otimes\Delta)\Theta)\Theta_{23},$$
coefficientwise in the transported source completion and on every vector for which the iterated actions are finite;

(iv) the bar-coproduct counterpart needed for the cocycle is
$$(\mathrm{id}\otimes\overline\Delta)\Theta_\nu=\sum_{\gamma+\eta=\nu}(\Theta_\gamma)_{13}(1\otimes K_{-\gamma}\otimes1)(\Theta_\eta)_{12}.$$

Removing the normalization $\Theta_0=1$ permits arbitrary scalar multiples of the same linear intertwiner equation, so normalization is essential for uniqueness; no integrality of coefficients and no uncontrolled infinite evaluation is asserted.

Let $\lambda\in P^+$, let $\pi_\lambda:U_q^-\to V(\lambda)$, $\pi_\lambda(P)=Pv_\lambda$, and let $G_\infty(b)$, $G_\lambda(\beta)$ be the lower global bases of $U_A^-$ and $V_A(\lambda)=U_A^-v_\lambda$ of [[def-lower-global-basis-of-a-quantum-highest-weight-module]]. Then:

(i) $\pi_\lambda:U_A^-\to V_A(\lambda)$ is a based quotient over $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$: $\pi_\lambda(G_\infty(b))=0$ if its crystal image $\pi_\lambda(b)\in\mathcal B(\lambda)\cup\{0\}$ is $0$, and $\pi_\lambda(G_\infty(b))=G_\lambda(\pi_\lambda(b))$ otherwise; consequently the kernel of $\pi_\lambda$ on $U_A^-$ is the $A$-span of exactly the killed lower global elements, the surviving elements map bijectively onto the integral highest-module basis $G_\lambda(\mathcal B(\lambda))$, the module weight components are finite free over $A$, and the compatible zero/infinity chart and residue projections have the crystal compatibility of the completed grand loop, all for every symmetrizable datum with the explicit label and auxiliary-realization convention;

(ii) more precisely, the integral kernel is
$$\ker\bigl(\pi_\lambda|_{U_A^-}\bigr)=\sum_{i\in I}\sum_{s>\lambda(h_i)}U_A^-F_i^{(s)}=\sum_{i\in I}\bigl(U_A^-\cap U_q^-F_i^{\lambda(h_i)+1}\bigr),$$
so the integral highest-module presentation uses all divided right powers beyond each highest limit, not just an ordinary power with a nonunit factorial.

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum and let $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra of [[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]], with $q_i=q^{d_i}$, $K_i:=K_{d_ih_i}$, coproduct $\Delta$, counit $\varepsilon$ and antipode $S$ as in [[thm-the-drinfeld-jimbo-formulas-define-a-hopf-algebra]]. Write $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ and let $U_A$, with generators $E_i^{(r)},F_i^{(r)},K_h^{\pm1},T_{i,c,t}$, be the Lusztig divided-power form of the receiving page. On the source side take Lusztig's presentation over $\mathbb Q(v)$, where $v$ is an indeterminate and $v_i=v^{d_i}$; the transport below sends $v_i$ to $q_i^{-1}$: generators $E_i^{L},F_i^{L},K_h^{L}$, the toral relations $K_h^{L}K_{h'}^{L}=K_{h+h'}^{L}$, $K_0^{L}=1$, the toral-action relations
$$K_h^{L}E_i^{L}=v^{\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}E_i^{L}K_h^{L},\qquad K_h^{L}F_i^{L}=v^{-\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}F_i^{L}K_h^{L},$$
the mixed relations $E_i^{L}F_j^{L}-F_j^{L}E_i^{L}=\delta_{ij}(K_i^{L}-(K_i^{L})^{-1})/(v_i-v_i^{-1})$, and the Serre relations with $v_i$-Gaussian binomial coefficients; let $\Delta_L$ be the source coproduct on generators
$$\Delta_L E_i^{L}=E_i^{L}\otimes1+K_i^{L}\otimes E_i^{L},\qquad \Delta_L F_i^{L}=F_i^{L}\otimes(K_i^{L})^{-1}+1\otimes F_i^{L},\qquad \Delta_L K_h^{L}=K_h^{L}\otimes K_h^{L}.$$
Let $B_K$ be the normalized Kashiwara half form on $U_q^-$ of [[thm-the-negative-half-bilinear-form-is-symmetric-nondegenerate-and-integral]], with skew derivations $e_i',e_i''$ of [[def-kashiwara-skew-derivations-on-the-negative-quantum-half]], and let $\psi$ be the bar involution of [[lem-the-lusztig-integral-form-is-stable-under-bar-and-contravariant-duality]]. Then:

(i) **Parameter transport.** The assignment $\varphi(v)=q^{-1}$, $\varphi(E_i^L)=E_i$, $\varphi(F_i^L)=F_i$, $\varphi(K_h^L)=K_{-h}$ defines an algebra isomorphism semilinear for the field isomorphism $\mathbb Q(v)\to\mathbb Q(q)$, $v\mapsto q^{-1}$. Its inverse sends $q\mapsto v^{-1}$ and $K_h\mapsto K_{-h}^L$, fixing the root generators. After the separate coefficient-renaming isomorphism $\rho:v\mapsto q$, $K_h^L\mapsto K_h$, this transport is $\varphi=\psi\rho$, with $\psi$ the library bar involution. It carries the source integral form onto $U_A$, fixes divided powers, inverts toral generators and fixes $T_{i,c,t}$. One must not apply the library bar a second time to the already transported parameter $v=q^{-1}$.

(ii) **Coproduct transport.** On all of the source algebra, $(\varphi\otimes\varphi)\circ\Delta_L=\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\circ\varphi$, where $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}=\mathrm{flip}\circ\Delta$. Equivalently the source coproduct is the opposite of the fixed library coproduct after parameter transport: the flip of the transported source coproduct is $\Delta$. In particular, with the barred coproduct $\bar\Delta(u):=(\psi\otimes\psi)\Delta(\psi(u))$, an element of the completed tensor square satisfying the source intertwining convention for $\Delta_L$ has a transport-flip that satisfies the library convention $\Delta(u)\Theta=\Theta\bar\Delta(u)$; this is the convention under which the normalized family of (vi) is read.

(iii) **The abstract half and its twisted product.** Transporting $\theta_i\mapsto F_i$ sends the source half $\mathbf f$ to $U_q^-$, the divided powers $\theta_i^{(n)}$ to $F_i^{(n)}$, and the source twisted coproduct multiplication $(x_1\otimes x_2)(y_1\otimes y_2)=v^{\langle\deg x_2,\deg y_1\rangle}x_1y_1\otimes x_2y_2$ to
$$(x_1\otimes x_2)(y_1\otimes y_2)=q^{-\langle\deg x_2,\deg y_1\rangle}x_1y_1\otimes x_2y_2$$
on $U_q^-\otimes U_q^-$; the coefficient extraction $e_i'(F_jQ)=\delta_{ij}Q+q_i^{-a_{ij}}F_je_i'(Q)$ of the transported twisted coproduct agrees with the library skew derivation $e_i'$.

(iv) **The half form up to the root-color factor.** On the homogeneous degree $\nu=\sum_i\nu_i\alpha_i$ the source form and the normalized Kashiwara form are related by
$$B_L=C_\nu\,B_K,\qquad C_\nu=\prod_i(1-q_i^2)^{-\nu_i},$$
a color-degree scaling which is a unit congruent to $1$ modulo $q$ and is not a single scalar on the whole half; for $P,Q$ of different degrees both sides vanish. In the rank-one subalgebra $B_L(F_i^{(n)},F_i^{(n)})=\prod_{r=1}^n(1-q_i^{2r})^{-1}$.

(v) **The normalized Drinfeld pairing.** Let $\iota:U_q^+\to U_q^-$ be the algebra isomorphism $E_i\mapsto F_i$. On homogeneous elements of opposite degrees set
$$D(x,y)=d_\nu^{-1}B_K(\iota x,y),\qquad d_\nu=\prod_i(q_i-q_i^{-1})^{\nu_i}\ \ (\deg x=\nu,\ \deg y=-\nu),$$
and set $D(x,y)=0$ for degrees not opposite. Then $D$ is a well-defined homogeneous pairing, perfect on every finite graded piece, and $D(E_i,F_j)=\delta_{ij}/(q_i-q_i^{-1})$; the pairing with generator value $1$ is the $B_K$-transport $B_K(\iota x,y)$. Its divided-power values are
$$D(E_i^{(n)},F_i^{(n)})=\frac{q_i^{-n(n-1)/2}}{[n]_i!\,(q_i-q_i^{-1})^n}.$$

(vi) **Quasi-R normalization.** In each degree $\nu$ let $(x_a),(y_b)$ be bases of $U_q^+[\nu]$ and $U_q^-[-\nu]$ and let $\Theta_\nu=\sum_a x_a\otimes y^a$ be the $D$-coevaluation, $y^a$ the $D$-dual basis. Then $\Theta_\nu$ is the transported, tensor-flipped source quasi-R component: the source coefficient of Lusztig's printed $\Theta$ is $(-1)^{\mathrm{ht}\,\nu}\prod_iv_i^{\nu_i}$ times the $B_L$-coevaluation, and after parameter transport and flip this scalar equals $d_\nu$, the scalar by which the $D$-coevaluation differs from the $B_K$-coevaluation. In particular, writing $[n]_{q_i^2}!=\prod_{r=1}^n(1+q_i^2+\cdots+q_i^{2(r-1)})$ (the geometric-sum factorial of the receiving page),
$$\Theta_{n\alpha_i}=(q_i-q_i^{-1})^n[n]_{q_i^2}!\,E_i^{(n)}\otimes F_i^{(n)},\qquad\text{so}\qquad \Theta_{\alpha_i}=(q_i-q_i^{-1})\,E_i\otimes F_i.$$

Let $\lambda\in P$ be a dominant integral label weight, put
$m_i:=\langle\lambda,h_i\rangle\ge0$, and let $M(\lambda)$ be the quantum Verma
module with highest vector $v_\lambda$
([[def-quantum-verma-module-and-simple-highest-weight-quotient]],
[[def-kac-moody-integral-and-dominant-integral-weights]]).

(i) The quotient $\tilde L(\lambda):=M(\lambda)/\sum_iU_q(\mathfrak g)F_i^{(m_i+1)}v_\lambda$
is nonzero, has finite-dimensional label weights and support contained in
$\lambda-Q_+$, is integrable, and equals the canonical simple highest weight
module $L(\lambda)$, which is simple also as an ordinary (not assumed graded)
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module.

(ii) **Universality.** Every integrable cyclic highest weight module $V$ of
highest weight $\lambda$ with highest vector $v\ne0$ receives a
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module map $\tilde L(\lambda)\to V$ with
$\bar v_\lambda\mapsto v$, and this map is unique; every nonzero such $V$ is
isomorphic to $L(\lambda)$.

(iii) Its character equals the classical integrable highest weight character of
the explicitly regularized realization of the datum. No global
$\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-freeness and no crystal or global basis is used.

Let $\lambda\in P$ be dominant integral, so $m_i:=\langle\lambda,h_i\rangle\ge0$
for all $i$, and let $M(\lambda)$ be the Verma module with highest vector
$v_\lambda$ ([[def-quantum-verma-module-and-simple-highest-weight-quotient]]).
Put $s_i:=F_i^{(m_i+1)}v_\lambda$.

(i) Every $s_i$ is a singular (highest weight) vector of weight
$\lambda-(m_i+1)\alpha_i$.

(ii) The graded submodule
$S:=\sum_iU_q(\mathfrak g)s_i=\sum_iU_q^-s_i$ is proper, and the quotient
$\tilde L(\lambda):=M(\lambda)/S$ is nonzero, has finite-dimensional
label-weight spaces, and is integrable ([[def-quantum-weight-module-and-integrability]]).

(iii) Every integrable cyclic highest weight module $V$ of highest weight
$\lambda$ is a quotient of $\tilde L(\lambda)$.

No commutation between divided powers $F_i^{(a)},F_j^{(b)}$ of distinct indices
with $a_{ij}\ne0$ is assumed anywhere.

Let $T$ and $I_{\mathrm{DJ}}$ be the free algebra and defining ideal of
[[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]], and put
$m_{ij}=1-a_{ij}$ and $\mathrm{Serre}^{\pm}_{ij}$ for its displayed Serre
sums. Define $\omega,\psi,\tau:T\to T$ on generators by

$$\omega(E_i)=-F_i,\quad\omega(F_i)=-E_i,\quad\omega(K_h)=K_{-h},$$

$$\psi(E_i)=E_i,\quad\psi(F_i)=F_i,\quad\psi(K_h)=K_{-h},$$

$$\tau(E_i)=F_i,\quad\tau(F_i)=E_i,\quad\tau(K_h)=K_{-h}.$$

Here $\omega$ fixes $\mathbb Q(q)$, while $\psi$ and $\tau$ apply the field
involution $q\mapsto q^{-1}$ to coefficients; $\omega$ and $\psi$ extend as
algebra maps, and $\tau$ extends as an anti-algebra map. Each map preserves
$I_{\mathrm{DJ}}$ and descends to $U_q(\mathfrak g)$. All three are
involutions; $\omega$ is a $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra automorphism, $\psi$ a
semilinear algebra automorphism, and $\tau$ a semilinear algebra
anti-involution. On the Serre sums,

$$\omega(\mathrm{Serre}^{\pm}_{ij})=(-1)^{a_{ij}}\mathrm{Serre}^{\mp}_{ij},\qquad\psi(\mathrm{Serre}^{\pm}_{ij})=\mathrm{Serre}^{\pm}_{ij},\qquad\tau(\mathrm{Serre}^{\pm}_{ij})=(-1)^{1-a_{ij}}\mathrm{Serre}^{\mp}_{ij}.$$

Let $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra of a finite symmetrizable Cartan datum, over $k=\mathbb Q(q)$, and let $U_q^-,U_q^0,U_q^+$ be its generated subalgebras of [[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]].

(i) Multiplication is a vector-space isomorphism
$$m:U_q^-\otimes_k U_q^0\otimes_k U_q^+\longrightarrow U_q(\mathfrak g),\qquad x_-\otimes x_0\otimes x_+\longmapsto x_-x_0x_+.$$
Products $b_-K_h b_+$, with $b_\pm$ ranging over supplied bases of the two halves and $h\in P^\vee$, form a basis of $U_q(\mathfrak g)$. Arbitrary simple-generator words span the halves; their Serre relations preclude claiming their independence.

(ii) The halves are exactly the algebras presented by their separate Serre relations, and $U_q^0\cong k[P^\vee]$. Thus all three abstract factor maps are injective and the $K_h$ are linearly independent.

(iii) For every $\beta\in Q$, the total root grading satisfies
$$U_q(\mathfrak g)[\beta]\cong\bigoplus_{\alpha,\gamma\in Q_+,\,\alpha-\gamma=\beta} U_q^-[-\gamma]\otimes_k U_q^0\otimes_k U_q^+[\alpha].$$
In particular degree zero contains all equal-positive/negative-degree summands, including $F_iE_i$; it is not just the toral subalgebra. As a left $U_q^0$-module this component is free, with rank equal to the possibly infinite sum of the products of the two half-component dimensions. Under AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the half-component dimensions are their classical PBW ranks, and products of the generic PBW bases of [[thm-generic-quantum-serre-halves-have-classical-pbw-ranks-and-a-nondegenerate-hopf-pairing]] with the toral basis give a PBW basis of the whole algebra. AC enters only through that supplier's formal-embedding proof; (i), (ii) and the graded tensor decomposition are choice-free.

Let $\Phi\subseteq E$ be a reduced crystallographic root system with positive
system $\Phi^{+}$, simple roots $\Delta=\{\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_r\}$ and Weyl
group $W$, with inversion sets $N(w)$ and lengths $\ell(w)=|N(w)|$
([[def-length-and-longest-element-of-a-finite-weyl-group]]). Then:
1. for every $w\in W$, the length $\ell(w)$ equals the minimum number of
   simple reflections occurring in an expression of $w$ as a product of simple
   reflections;
2. there is a unique longest element $w_0\in W$; it satisfies
   $w_0(\Phi^{+})=\Phi^{-}$ and $\ell(w_0)=|\Phi^{+}|$.

Use the actual periodic based $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ module and its finite cuts of [[lem-two-cyclotomic-shears-give-a-periodic-integrable-based-sl-two-chain]]. Thus $n_{2k}=8k+2$, $n_{2k+1}=8k+4$, $p=q+q^{-1}$, $h=q^2+q^{-2}$, and $M^{(J)}$ keeps constituents $0,\ldots,J$ and shears only at indices less than $J$. On $(M^{(J)})^{\otimes2}$ let $\Psi_J=\Theta(\psi\otimes\psi)$ be the actual rank-one tensor bar, and put $e^{(J)}=b_{0,0}\otimes b_{0,2}$. Every sum and vector here is algebraic.

For each $J\ge1$, there is a unique $\Psi_J$-fixed vector $g^{(J)}$ with seed coefficient $1$ and strictly increasing first-weight corrections in $q\mathbb Z[q]$. For every odd $j=2k+1\le J$, its coefficient $F_j(q)$ at $b_{j,0}\otimes b_{j,n_j}$ is independent of $J$ and satisfies

$$F_{2k+1}(q)\equiv(-1)^k(2k+1)!(q^3-q)\pmod{q^4+1}.$$

In particular this coefficient is nonzero. Every cut $J\ge1$ therefore has a nonzero corrected coordinate with constituent index at least $J-1$. For $L\ge J$, retaining the raw coordinates with both indices at most $J$ sends $g^{(L)}$ exactly to $g^{(J)}$, including at the last retained constituent where its outgoing shear has been omitted. No choice assumption is used.

derivations.claim: **Highest-first integral action.** Let $m=F_i^{(r)}m'$ be a homogeneous divided word of first height $h$, with $r\ge1$, and let $n\in N_A$. The base $v_\lambda\otimes n$ is preserved integrally by $\Psi$, since all positive components kill $v_\lambda$. For $t\ge1$ put $z_t=F_i^{(r-t)}m'\otimes F_i^{(t)}n$ and $a_t=q_i^{t(\mu(h_i)-r+t)}\in A$, where $m'$ has weight $\mu$. Formula [F1] gives $\Delta(F_i^{(r)})(m'\otimes n)=m\otimes n+\sum_{t=1}^ra_tz_t$. Semilinearity and bar compatibility give the exact recursion $\Psi(m\otimes n)=\Delta(F_i^{(r)})\Psi(m'\otimes n)-\sum_{t=1}^r\bar a_t\Psi(z_t)$. All tensors on the right have first height less than $h$, so induction makes their bars integral; the coproduct preserves the integral tensor lattice by [F1]. Divided words span $V_A(\lambda)$, hence $\Psi$ is integral on the whole tensor lattice. The factor bar is an integral bijection, so $\Theta$ is integral as well. The action is finite because first-factor raising is bounded by its highest cone.

**Lowest-second action (b).** Dually, let $\omega V(\lambda)$ be the lowest module and $M$ based. The second coproduct identity of [F1] has $t=0$ term $1\otimes E_i^{(r)}$ raising only the second factor with coefficient $1$; the $t\ge1$ terms carry smaller second divided-word height and toral factors $q_i^{t(r-t)}$ acting with the weights of the first factor, again $A$-units. The same induction on the second divided-word height, now with the fixed bar of the lowest vector, proves that $\Psi$ preserves $M_A\otimes\omega V_A(\lambda)$; the explicit lower-cone bound of the based class makes the action vectorwise finite before any completed series is evaluated. This proves (b).

**Finite-type action finiteness without multiplicity bounds.** First an integrable upper-cone module has reflection-stable label support: a nonzero admissible string position at label $\eta$ with top $\eta+n\alpha_i$ and top coroot $a=\langle\eta,h_iangle+2n$ has a nonzero mirrored position $a-n$ of label $\eta-\langle\eta,h_iangle\alpha_i$. The map $U^+	o U^+m$, $u\mapsto um$, kills $\sum_iU^+E_i^{(\langle\lambda,h_iangle+1)}$, and by the half-exchange and highest presentation in [F5] its quotient is a copy of the finite-dimensional negative-half highest quotient as a vector space. **The constructed highest and lowest classes (d).** Form right-associated products of highest modules. Highest-first action proves integrality of the normalized bar at every binary step, while the field cocycle of [F2] gives all parenthesizations the same bar without assuming integral action for intermediate arbitrary pairs. In the transfer order in which each positive-root component raises the first weight and lowers the second, only the degree-$0$ component fixes a label pair, so the bar is triangular with diagonal $1$. Every upward interval is finite by the upper-cone or finite-total-weight hypothesis, and for the lowest classes the lower-cone bound replaces finiteness of the whole mixed weight space. In a finite interval solve for a bar-fixed lift $g_t=e_t+\sum_{s>t}a_{ts}e_s$ with $a_{ts}\in q\mathbb Z[q]$, starting from the top: after subtracting the already constructed larger lifts, involutivity makes the remainder satisfy $f+\bar f=0$, whose unique positive $q$-part supplies the next correction. **Closure under tensor constructions and based subquotients.** For a highest tensor object $P=V(\lambda_1)\otimes\cdots\otimes V(\lambda_m)$ and any based $N$, right-associate $P\otimes N$. Repeated highest-first action from step 1.1 makes every binary bar integral. The mirror argument uses step 1.2 for arbitrary first factor and a lowest tensor object. This includes pairs of constructed objects and proves the arbitrary-other-factor cases before inheritance. Based subobjects are spanned by subsets of the actual constructed bases and are therefore saturated, $(P_A\otimes Q_A)\cap(P'\otimes Q')=P'_A\otimes Q'_A$; $\Theta$ preserves their field submodules by its $U$-monomial terms, so integral action follows from the equality. Let $U_q^-$ be the negative half of the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra with its
Kashiwara skew derivations $e_i',e_i''$
([[def-kashiwara-skew-derivations-on-the-negative-quantum-half]]), let
$A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ and let $U_A^-$ be the divided-power half generated by
the $F_i^{(r)}$ ([[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]]). Then:

(i) $e_i'$ preserves $U_A^-$: $e_i'(U_A^-)\subseteq U_A^-$.

(ii) Define, for $x\in U_q^-$,
$$P_ix:=\sum_{n\ge0}(-1)^nq_i^{-n(n-1)/2}\,F_i^{(n)}(e_i')^n x,$$
the sum being finite on each $x$ because $e_i'$ is locally nilpotent, and the
powers $(e_i')^n$ being ordinary, not divided, powers of the derivation. Then
$P_i$ is a well-defined $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear map with $e_i'P_i=0$ that fixes
$\ker e_i'$ pointwise and annihilates $F_iU_q^-$; hence
$U_q^-=\ker e_i'\oplus F_iU_q^-$ and $P_i$ is the projection onto $\ker e_i'$
along $F_iU_q^-$.

(iii) Every $x\in U_A^-$ has a unique finite expansion
$$x=\sum_{n\ge0}F_i^{(n)}x_n,\qquad e_i'x_n=0,$$
with $x_n=q_i^{n(n-1)/2}P_i(e_i')^nx\in U_A^-$ for every $n$; the sum is finite
because $(e_i')^nx=0$ for large $n$. Consequently the string operators
$\tilde e_i\bigl(\sum_nF_i^{(n)}x_n\bigr):=\sum_{n\ge1}F_i^{(n-1)}x_n$ and
$\tilde f_i\bigl(\sum_nF_i^{(n)}x_n\bigr):=\sum_{n\ge0}F_i^{(n+1)}x_n$
preserve $U_A^-$.

No global $A$-basis and no freeness of $U_A^-$ over $A$ is assumed or asserted.

Let $U_q^-$ be the negative half of the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra with its skew derivations $e_i',e_i'':U_q^-\to U_q^-$ ([[def-kashiwara-skew-derivations-on-the-negative-quantum-half]], [[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]), fix $i\in I$, and write $f_i^{(n)}=F_i^n/[n]_i!$ for the divided powers ([[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]). Then:

(i) $e_i'$ is locally nilpotent on $U_q^-$, and the endomorphism
$$P_i:=\sum_{m\ge0}(-1)^mq_i^{-m(m-1)/2}F_i^{(m)}e_i'^{\,m}\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb Q(q)}(U_q^-)$$
is well defined (each sum is finite on each element) and is the projection onto $\operatorname{Ker}e_i'$ along $f_iU_q^-$. In particular $e_i'P_i=0$, $P_iF_i=0$, $P_i^2=P_i$, $P_iu=u$ for $u\in\operatorname{Ker}e_i'$, and
$$U_q^-=\operatorname{Ker}e_i'\oplus f_iU_q^-.$$

(ii) Every $u\in U_q^-$ has a unique $i$-string decomposition
$$u=\sum_{n\ge0}f_i^{(n)}u_n,\qquad u_n\in\operatorname{Ker}e_i',\qquad u_n=0\ \text{for }n\gg0,$$
and the components are given by $u_n=q_i^{n(n-1)/2}P_ie_i'^{\,n}u$.

(iii) The **Kashiwara operators on the negative half**, defined on the string decomposition by
$$\tilde e_iu:=\sum_{n\ge1}f_i^{(n-1)}u_n,\qquad \tilde f_iu:=\sum_{n\ge0}f_i^{(n+1)}u_n,$$
are $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear endomorphisms of $U_q^-$ with $\tilde e_i\tilde f_i=\operatorname{id}_{U_q^-}$; $\tilde e_iu=0$ if and only if $u\in\operatorname{Ker}e_i'$; $\tilde f_i$ is injective and $\tilde f_i(1)=F_i$. Both operators preserve the root grading and shift its degree by $\mp\alpha_i$, that is $\tilde e_i(U_q^-[-\nu])\subseteq U_q^-[-\nu+\alpha_i]$ and $\tilde f_i(U_q^-[-\nu])\subseteq U_q^-[-\nu-\alpha_i]$.

No choice principle is used. Here $e_i'^{\,n}$ denotes the ordinary $n$-fold power of the derivation, not its divided power. The same projector and every string coefficient preserve the $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ divided-power lattice $U_A^-$ ([[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]]), as proved by the integral skew-string supplier; this does not assert that lattice's freeness.

Let $\mathcal L(\infty)\subseteq U_q^-$ and $\mathcal B(\infty)\subseteq\mathcal L(\infty)/q\mathcal L(\infty)$ be the Kashiwara lattice and generating set of [[def-kashiwara-lattices-lambda-and-infinity]], with the Kashiwara operators $\tilde e_i,\tilde f_i$ on $U_q^-$ of [[thm-the-i-string-decomposition-of-the-negative-half]](iii).

(i) $(\mathcal L(\infty),\mathcal B(\infty))$ is a crystal basis of $U_q^-$ in the sense of [[def-crystal-lattice-and-crystal-basis]]: $\mathcal L(\infty)$ is a free $A_0$-submodule with $U_q^-\cong\mathbb Q(q)\otimes_{A_0}\mathcal L(\infty)$, stable under $\tilde e_i$ and $\tilde f_i$; and $\mathcal B(\infty)$ is a $\mathbb Q$-basis of $\mathcal L(\infty)/q\mathcal L(\infty)$ satisfying $\tilde e_i\mathcal B(\infty)\subseteq\mathcal B(\infty)\cup\{0\}$, $\tilde f_i\mathcal B(\infty)\subseteq\mathcal B(\infty)$, and $\tilde f_ib=b'$ if and only if $b=\tilde e_ib'$ for all $b,b'\in\mathcal B(\infty)$.

(iv) The root-graded crystal has finite $\varepsilon_i$ on each element, formal $\varphi_i=\varepsilon_i+\langle h_i,\mathrm{wt}\rangle$, and actual lowering length $\ell_i^-=\infty$. Every $\tilde f_i$-iterate is nonzero because $\tilde e_i\tilde f_i=\mathrm{id}$ holds on its lattice and residue. Thus it is the infinite lowering crystal of the unit, with the negative-half convention of the crystal-graph definition.

**Choice.** The axiom of choice is declared via [[def-axiom-of-choice]] and enters only through the grand loop: the partial-inverse axiom in (i) uses clause J(r) of [[thm-grand-loop-existence-of-highest-weight-crystal-bases]], whose proof consumes the AC-dependent form comparison of the negative-half form. The freeness and rank statements are choice-free.

Let $\lambda\in P^+$ and let $\mathcal L(\lambda),\mathcal B(\lambda),\mathcal L(\infty),\mathcal B(\infty)$ be the lattices and bases of [[def-kashiwara-lattices-lambda-and-infinity]], with $\pi_\lambda:U_q^-\to V(\lambda)$, $P\mapsto Pv_\lambda$, and Kashiwara operators $\tilde e_i,\tilde f_i$. Then for every $\alpha\in Q_+$, every $i\in I$ and every $\lambda\in P^+$:

(a) **Lattice projection.** $\pi_\lambda(\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha})=\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$.

(c) **Basis projection.** The map induced by $\pi_\lambda$ is a bijection $\{b\in\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\alpha}:\pi_\lambda(b)\neq0\}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal B(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$.

Then the image of this injection is exactly $\bigoplus_{b\in\mathcal B(\infty)}\mathbb Z b$; in particular $L_{\mathbb Z}/qL_{\mathbb Z}$ is a free $\mathbb Z$-module with basis $\mathcal B(\infty)$, and after tensoring with $\mathbb Q$ it is the full rational crystal space $\mathbb Q\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\bigoplus_b\mathbb Zb=\mathcal L(\infty)/q\mathcal L(\infty)$.

The normalized Kashiwara half form of [[thm-the-negative-half-bilinear-form-is-symmetric-nondegenerate-and-integral]] takes values on $U_A^-$ in $K_{\mathbb Z}=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1},(1-q^{2n})^{-1}:n\ge1]$ and on $L_{\mathbb Z}$ in $A_{\mathbb Z}=\mathbb Z[q,(1-q^{2n})^{-1}:n\ge1]$; consequently its residue pairing on $L_{\mathbb Z}/qL_{\mathbb Z}$ is $\mathbb Z$-valued. In the residue basis $\mathcal B(\infty)$ the coefficients of an integral element are its integer pairings with the basis vectors, and the norm-$1$ elements of the integral residue $L_{\mathbb Z}/qL_{\mathbb Z}$ are exactly $\mathcal B(\infty)\cup(-\mathcal B(\infty))$. The Kashiwara operators $\tilde e_i,\tilde f_i$ preserve $L_{\mathbb Z}$, hence induce endomorphisms of the integral residue subgroup. No $A$-module structure on $L_{\mathbb Z}$, no identification of the integral residue with the rational residue as a $\mathbb Z$-module, and no unsigned norm-$1$ characterization is asserted; the module integral residue basis is established only in the globalization theorem of this page.

Fix a symmetrizable Cartan datum and $i\in I$, and use the conventions of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]. Write $C_{m,r}:=\binom{m}{r}_i$, with $C_{m,r}=0$ when $r<0$ or $r>m$.

(i) **Pascal recurrences.** For $m\ge1$ and every integer $r$,

$$C_{m,r}=q_i^{-r}C_{m-1,r}+q_i^{m-r}C_{m-1,r-1}=q_i^rC_{m-1,r}+q_i^{r-m}C_{m-1,r-1}.$$

(ii) **Symmetry.** For $0\le r\le m$, $C_{m,r}=C_{m,m-r}$.

(iii) **Gauss product formula.** For every $N\ge0$, in the polynomial ring $\mathbb Q(q)[z]$,

$$\prod_{j=0}^{N-1}(1+q_i^{2j}z)=\sum_{r=0}^{N}q_i^{r(N-1)}C_{N,r}z^r.$$

Consequently, for $N\ge1$,

$$\sum_{r=0}^{N}(-1)^rq_i^{r(N-1)}C_{N,r}=0.$$

(iv) **Integrality.** For $0\le r\le m$,

$$C_{m,r}\in q_i^{-r(m-r)}\mathbb Z[q_i^2]\subseteq\mathbb Z[q_i^{\pm1}].$$

Thus every Gaussian quotient is a Laurent polynomial in $q_i$ with integer coefficients, and the Pascal recurrences hold in that Laurent polynomial ring.

Let $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra of
[[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]], with its generated
subalgebras $U_q^-,U_q^0,U_q^+$ and root gradings
$U_q^-=\bigoplus_{\nu\in Q_+}U_q^-[-\nu]$ of
[[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]
($Q_+=\bigoplus_i\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\alpha_i$, height $\operatorname{ht}$ of
[[def-kac-moody-root-lattice-height-and-positive-cone]]). Fix $i\in I$ and
write $K_i:=K_{d_ih_i}$, so that $K_iF_jK_i^{-1}=q_i^{-a_{ij}}F_j$ and
$q_i-q_i^{-1}\ne0$.

For every $P\in U_q^-$ there exist unique elements $Q,R\in U_q^-$ with

$$E_iP-PE_i=\frac{K_iQ-K_i^{-1}R}{q_i-q_i^{-1}}.$$

Define the **Kashiwara skew derivations** $e_i',e_i'':U_q^-\to U_q^-$ by

$$e_i'(P):=R\qquad\text{and}\qquad e_i''(P):=Q .$$

Thus $e_i'$ is the operator whose value is the coefficient of $K_i^{-1}$ and
$e_i''$ is the operator whose value is the coefficient of $K_i$ in the
commutator with $E_i$. The maps have the following properties, all proved in
the Verification below.

(a) $e_i'$ and $e_i''$ are $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear, vanish on $1$, and
$e_i'(F_j)=e_i''(F_j)=\delta_{ij}$ for all $j\in I$.

(b) (Twisted Leibniz rules) For homogeneous $x,y\in U_q^-$, with the actual
weight $\operatorname{wt}(x)\in Q$ of [[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]],
$$e_i'(xy)=e_i'(x)y+q_i^{\langle\operatorname{wt}(x),h_i\rangle}x\,e_i'(y),\qquad e_i''(xy)=e_i''(x)y+q_i^{-\langle\operatorname{wt}(x),h_i\rangle}x\,e_i''(y).$$

(c) (Commutation with the generators) For all $j\in I$ and all $y\in U_q^-$,
$$e_i'(F_jy)=q_i^{-a_{ij}}F_j\,e_i'(y)+\delta_{ij}y,\qquad e_i''(F_jy)=q_i^{a_{ij}}F_j\,e_i''(y)+\delta_{ij}y,$$

equivalently $e_i'F_j=q_i^{-a_{ij}}F_je_i'+\delta_{ij}$ and
$e_i''F_j=q_i^{a_{ij}}F_je_i''+\delta_{ij}$ as operators on $U_q^-$.

(d) (Grading, height and nilpotence) For every $\nu\in Q_+$,

$$e_i'\bigl(U_q^-[-\nu]\bigr),\ e_i''\bigl(U_q^-[-\nu]\bigr)\ \subseteq\ U_q^-[ -(\nu-\alpha_i)],$$

the right-hand side being $0$ when $\nu-\alpha_i\notin Q_+$. In particular both
maps raise the actual weight by $\alpha_i$, lower the positive height by one,
and are locally nilpotent: $(e_i')^{k}(P)=(e_i'')^{k}(P)=0$ for $k$ larger than
the height of the degree of a homogeneous $P$.

(e) (Bar compatibility) Let $\psi$ be the semilinear algebra involution
$q\mapsto q^{-1}$, $E_i\mapsto E_i$, $F_i\mapsto F_i$, $K_h\mapsto K_{-h}$ of
[[lem-quantum-serre-relations-are-stable-under-the-chevalley-involutions]].
Then $e_i''=\psi\,e_i'\,\psi$ on $U_q^-$.

The commutator construction also fixes the orientation: the
$K_i^{-1}$-coefficient is $e_i'$ and the $K_i$-coefficient is $e_i''$. The
twists $q_i^{\pm\langle\operatorname{wt}(x),h_i\rangle}$ in (b) are the twists
of the corresponding coefficient maps of the negative-half coproduct in the
source's dictionary; the explicit commutator computation used here is the
definition of record, and no imaginary-simple-root convention is needed, since
every Cartan datum of this library has $a_{ii}=2$.

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum for a quantum
group with $a_{ii}=2$ for all $i$
([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]), let
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be its Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra
([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]) with $q_i=q^{d_i}$ and
$K_i=K_{d_ih_i}$, and set

$$A:=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]\ \subseteq\ \mathbb Q(q),$$

the image of the Laurent polynomial ring $\Lambda_1=\mathbb Z[t]_{S}$ of
[[def-the-laurent-polynomial-ring]] under the unital ring homomorphism sending
$t$ to the indeterminate $q$; this homomorphism is injective and $A$ is a
subring of $\mathbb Q(q)$ (Verification, step 1.1). We work over this
commutative domain $A$ inside the field $\mathbb Q(q)$.

For $i\in I$, $c\in\mathbb Z$ and $t\ge0$ define the **toral quantum binomial**

$$T_{i,c,t}:=\begin{bmatrix}K_i;c\\ t\end{bmatrix}:=\prod_{s=1}^{t}\frac{K_iq_i^{\,c-s+1}-K_i^{-1}q_i^{\,-c+s-1}}{q_i^{\,s}-q_i^{\,-s}}\in U_q(\mathfrak g),$$

the empty product being $T_{i,c,0}:=1$. Each factor is defined in
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$ because $q_i^{\,s}-q_i^{\,-s}\ne0$ for $s\ge1$
([[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]), so
$T_{i,c,t}$ is a polynomial in $K_i^{\pm1}$ with coefficients in $\mathbb Q(q)$;
in particular all $T_{i,c,t}$ commute with the $K_h$ and with one another
(Verification, step 2.1).

The **Lusztig divided-power integral form** is the $A$-subalgebra

$$U_A:=\bigl\langle E_i^{(r)},\ F_i^{(r)},\ K_h^{\pm1},\ T_{i,c,t}\ \colon\ i\in I,\ r,t\ge0,\ c\in\mathbb Z,\ h\in P^{\vee}\bigr\rangle\ \subseteq\ U_q(\mathfrak g),$$

where $x^{(r)}=x^r/[r]_i!$ are the divided powers of
[[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]. Write $U_A^\pm$
for the $A$-subalgebras generated by the $E_i^{(r)}$ and by the $F_i^{(r)}$,
and $U_A^0$ for the one generated by the $K_h^{\pm1}$ and the $T_{i,c,t}$.

Then:

(i) $U_A$ contains $E_i=E_i^{(1)}$, $F_i=F_i^{(1)}$ and all $K_h$;

(ii) $U_A$ is a root-graded $A$-subalgebra of the root-graded
$\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ ([[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]):
with $U_A[\beta]:=U_A\cap U_q(\mathfrak g)[\beta]$ one has
$U_A=\bigoplus_{\beta\in Q}U_A[\beta]$, each $U_A[\beta]$ is an $A$-submodule,
and $U_A^\pm,U_A^0$ are graded in the same way;

(iii) $U_A\otimes_A\mathbb Q(q)\cong U_q(\mathfrak g)$ canonically, i.e. the
$\mathbb Q(q)$-span of $U_A$ is all of $U_q(\mathfrak g)$.

The shifted binomials $T_{i,c,t}$ with $c\ne0$ are included because the
divided-power reordering identity of
[[lem-divided-power-and-toral-quantum-binomial-reordering-identities]] has
coefficients $T_{i,2t-a-b,t}$ with a nonconstant index; the specializations at
$q=1$ of these elements are computed in
[[lem-q-one-toral-specialization-identifies-the-classical-cartan-generators]],
and the integral triangular decomposition and the specialization are treated
only after this definition.

No freeness of $U_A$ or of its parts over $A$, no independence of the listed
generators, and no triangularity of the products of the three parts is asserted
here. In particular $A$ is not a principal ideal domain (Verification, step
7.1), so no torsion-free-to-free inference over $A$ is permitted anywhere on
this page.

Let $\lambda\in P^+$ and let $L(\lambda)$ be the simple integrable highest weight module with highest weight vector $v_\lambda$ ([[thm-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module-exists-and-is-unique]]); in this page we write $V(\lambda):=L(\lambda)$, following the notation of the crystal sources. Let $U_q^-$ be the negative half with its Kashiwara operators $\tilde e_i,\tilde f_i$ ([[thm-the-i-string-decomposition-of-the-negative-half]]), and let $A_0$ be the crystal limiting ring ([[def-the-local-ring-at-q-zero]]).

Define $\mathcal L(\lambda)$ to be the $A_0$-submodule of $V(\lambda)$ generated by all vectors $\tilde f_{i_1}\cdots\tilde f_{i_r}v_\lambda$ ($r\ge0$, $i_1,\dots,i_r\in I$), where for $r=0$ the vector is $v_\lambda$; and $\mathcal L(\infty)$ to be the $A_0$-submodule of $U_q^-$ generated by all $\tilde f_{i_1}\cdots\tilde f_{i_r}\mathbf 1$ ($r\ge0$), where $\mathbf 1$ is the unit of $U_q^-$. Here $\tilde f_i$ on $V(\lambda)$ are the module Kashiwara operators and $\tilde f_i$ on $U_q^-$ are the negative-half operators. Define
$$\mathcal B(\lambda):=\{\tilde f_{i_1}\cdots\tilde f_{i_r}v_\lambda+q\mathcal L(\lambda):r\ge0\}\setminus\{0\}\subseteq\mathcal L(\lambda)/q\mathcal L(\lambda),$$
$$\mathcal B(\infty):=\{\tilde f_{i_1}\cdots\tilde f_{i_r}\mathbf 1+q\mathcal L(\infty):r\ge0\}\setminus\{0\}\subseteq\mathcal L(\infty)/q\mathcal L(\infty).$$

Then, with $\pi_\lambda:U_q^-\to V(\lambda)$, $\pi_\lambda(P)=Pv_\lambda$:

(a) $\mathcal L(\lambda)=\bigoplus_{\mu\in P}\mathcal L(\lambda)_\mu$ with $\mathcal L(\lambda)_\mu=\mathcal L(\lambda)\cap V(\lambda)_\mu$, and $\mathcal L(\infty)=\bigoplus_{\nu\in Q_+}\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\nu}$ with $\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\nu}=\mathcal L(\infty)\cap U_q^-[-\nu]$; correspondingly $\mathcal B(\lambda)=\bigsqcup_\mu\mathcal B(\lambda)_\mu$ and $\mathcal B(\infty)=\bigsqcup_\nu\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\nu}$.

(b) $\tilde f_i\mathcal L(\lambda)\subseteq\mathcal L(\lambda)$ and $\tilde f_i\mathcal L(\infty)\subseteq\mathcal L(\infty)$.

(c) (Recursive spanning.) For $\alpha\in Q_+\setminus\{0\}$,
$$\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}=\sum_{i\in I}\tilde f_i\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha+\alpha_i},\qquad \mathcal B(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}=\Bigl(\bigcup_{i\in I}\tilde f_i\mathcal B(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha+\alpha_i}\Bigr)\setminus\{0\},$$
and the same formulas with $\mathcal L(\infty),\mathcal B(\infty)$. Each $\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$ and each $\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha}$ is generated over $A_0$ by finitely many monomials of total length at most $\operatorname{ht}(\alpha)$, hence is a finitely generated $A_0$-module.

No basis property, scalar-extension spanning or crystal-lattice property of $\mathcal L(\lambda)$ or $\mathcal L(\infty)$ is asserted here; these are conclusions of the grand loop. The script letters avoid the collision with the simple module $L(\lambda)$. No choice principle is used. Each fixed component is torsionfree inside a field vector space and generated by finitely many words of its fixed height, so it is free over the DVR $A_0$; its full field-span is proved later. The field map $\pi_\lambda$ is surjective, but exact equality on Kashiwara monomial generators is not asserted.

derivations.claim: **The integral string decomposition and projector.** For $u\in U_A^-$ the unique decomposition of [F2] has $u_l=q_i^{l(l-1)/2}P_i(e_i')^lu$ with $P_i=\sum_l(-1)^lq_i^{-l(l-1)/2}F_i^{(l)}(e_i')^l$, the powers of $e_i'$ being ordinary; by [F1] the coefficients $q_i^{\pm l(l-1)/2}$ and the operators $F_i^{(l)}$ and $(e_i')^l$ preserve $U_A^-$, so every $u_l$ lies in $U_A^-$.

**The finite Gaussian identity.** Fix integers $m\ge n\ge1$, put $z=q_i$, $Q=z^2$, define $(Q;Q)_r:=\prod_{j=1}^r(1-Q^j)$ for $r\ge0$, and set $H(t)=\prod_{j=1}^{n-1}(1-Q^{-j}t)\prod_{j=1}^{m-n}(1-Q^jt)$, a polynomial of degree $m-1$. For every polynomial of degree $\le m-1$ the finite $q$-binomial theorem of [F5] gives $\sum_{k=0}^m(-1)^kQ^{k(k-1)/2-k(m-1)}\binom{m}{k}_QH(Q^k)=0$: on the monomial $t^s$ the sum factors as $\prod_{j=0}^{m-1}(1-Q^{j+s-m+1})$, which contains the zero factor $j=m-1-s$. For $1\le k<n$ one has $H(Q^k)=0$; for $k\ge n$, $H(Q^k)/[(Q;Q)_{n-1}(Q;Q)_{m-n}]=\binom{k-1}{n-1}_Q\binom{m-n+k}{k}_Q$; and the $k=0$ term equals $(-1)^{n-1}Q^{-n(n-1)/2}$. Multiplying the vanishing sum by $(-1)^nQ^{n(n-1)/2}$ divided by the two factorials turns it into $\sum_{k=n}^m(-1)^{k-n}\binom{k-1}{k-n}_z\binom{m-n+k}{k}_z\binom{m}{k}_z=1$, using $\binom{a}{b}_z=z^{-b(a-b)}\binom{a}{b}_Q$ and the exponent identity $k(k-1)/2-k(m-1)+n(n-1)/2=-\frac{(n-1)(k-n)+k(m-n)+k(m-k)}2$.

**String ideals.** By [F2], $u\in F_i^nU_q^-$ if and only if $u_l=0$ for $l<n$; hence $I_{(i,n)}=U_A^-\cap F_i^nU_q^-$ equals $\bigoplus_{l\ge n}F_i^{(l)}(\ker e_i'\cap U_A^-)$ directly, and this equals the sum $\sum_{l\ge n}F_i^{(l)}U_A^-$ because each displayed direct summand is contained in $F_i^{(l)}U_A^-$, while multiplying an integral string expansion by $F_i^{(l)}$ yields only positions $l+m\ge l$ with integral coefficients $\binom{l+m}{l}_i$; the sum is not direct as written. Applying the $A$-linear projection $\pi_\lambda$ of [[def-integral-residue-lattices-of-the-negative-half-and-highest-weight-modules]] gives $J_{(i,n)}^A=\sum_{l\ge n}F_i^{(l)}V_A(\lambda)$, an $A$-submodule of the field subspace $F_i^nV(\lambda)$, with no $U_q$- or $U_A$-stability asserted.

**Boundary generation on a module lattice.** By [[thm-unique-kashiwara-i-string-decomposition]], reduce to an admissible string vector $u=F_i^{(m)}v$ with $E_iv=0$ and top weight $2m-n$. Admissibility gives $m\le2m-n$, hence $m\ge n$; the formulas of [[thm-quantized-sl-two-string-formulas]] give $F_i^{(k)}E_i^{(k)}u=\binom{m-n+k}{k}_z\binom{m}{k}_zu$ for $k\le m$ and $0$ for $k>m$. Substituting step 1.2, the alternating sum of step (iv) is $u$: the coefficients are exactly those of the proved identity, with finite support because $k\le m$. Every $u\in(M_A)_\mu$ is a finite sum of such string vectors, and all operators and coefficients involved lie in $A$ and preserve $M_A$ ([[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]]), so $(M_A)_\mu=\sum_{k\ge n}F_i^{(k)}(M_A)_{\mu+k\alpha_i}$, with finiteness supplied by integrability.

**String-ideal residues.** By [F2], the field image of $\tilde f_i^n$ is $F_i^nU_q^-$. On this image $\tilde f_i^n\tilde e_i^n$ is the identity. Both shifts preserve $U_A^-$ and $\mathcal L(\infty)$ by [F1], [F3], so $I_{(i,n)}^A\cap\mathcal L(\infty)=\tilde f_i^n L_{\mathbb Z}$. Taking residues and using [F4] gives exactly the integral span of $\tilde f_i^n\mathcal B(\infty)$; the same argument over $A_0$ gives its rational span.

**Conclusion.** Steps 1.1–2.1 prove (i) and (ii), step 3.1 proves (iii), step 2.2 proves (iv); integral balancedness of the string-ideal triple is left to the subsequent induction and no saturation of $J_{(i,n)}^A$, no $U_q$-structure on it and no divided-derivation integrality are asserted.
